panels.title: svc-voice: its event loop (the stall alarm) and its keep-warm
Loop held 5 s+, and stack dumps (5 min)
panels.description: svc-voice's watchdog, in each 5 minutes: its loop's timer firing five seconds or more late (`voice_loop_lag_over_5s`), and faulthandler's stack dumps, one per thread, written once the loop has not beaten for five seconds whether or not it came back (`voice_stack_dumps`). Above 0 of either opens `voice-loop-stall`: a caller hears dead air. Nothing of a call is on the lines.

panels.title: Loop held 1 s+ (5 min)
panels.description: The loop's timer firing a second or more late (`voice_loop_lag_over_1s`), in each 5 minutes. The red line is `voice-loop-stall`'s: above 2 (three or more) opens it.

panels.title: How late its timer fired (p99, p50)
panels.description: Each late timer's lag (`voice_loop_lag_ms`, a line's `lag_ms`): nothing drawn, no timer fired late. No policy reads the distribution; it is for reading a stall afterwards.

panels.title: Late timers, by where
panels.description: Every late-timer line (`voice_loop_lag`) by its closed `where` code: the kind of stall.

panels.title: Keep-warm steps that failed, by step (15 min)
panels.description: svc-voice's failed or timed-out keep-warm steps (`voice_keep_warm_failures`), by step, in each 15 minutes. The red line is `voice-keep-warm-failing`'s: above 3 of one step opens it; that path is cold for the next call.

panels.title: Resources: each Cloud Run service's CPU, memory, instances, concurrency and start-up (open a row)
No disk on a Cloud Run service

options.content: **Cloud Run services have no disk.** A file a container writes is held in its memory, so a service's "disk space" is its **Memory** chart: files that grow show as memory climbing to the red line, then as a container killed for memory. Real disk is on the databases (each one's disk space is on its area's page and on Databases) and in the buckets. A **red line** is the line the pager uses (tpa-platform's alert policies); a **grey line** is a limit the service is set to.

panels.title: Resources · svc-voice: CPU, memory, instances, concurrency, start-up
CPU (p99, p95, p50)
panels.description: svc-voice's container CPU, the share of its CPU limit in use (`container/cpu/utilizations`): the 99th, 95th and 50th percentile across its instances in each 5-minute window. The red line is `run-cpu-high`'s: the p99 above 90% for 15 minutes pages (instances saturated: requests queue and slow).

links.title: svc-voice: CPU, memory, instances, concurrency, start-up

panels.title: Memory (p99, p95, p50)
panels.description: svc-voice's container memory, the share of its memory limit in use (`container/memory/utilizations`), percentiles across its instances in each 5-minute window. Cloud Run has no disk: files the container writes are held in memory and count here. The red line is `run-memory-high`'s: the p99 above 90% for 10 minutes pages; at the limit the container is killed (`run-oom`, the last panel of this row).

panels.title: Instances (total, active, idle)
panels.description: svc-voice's Cloud Run instances: the total, the most in each minute summed over active and idle, as the `ceiling-` policies read it, and active (serving or starting) and idle (kept warm, or waiting to be shut down) apart. @@E@@This environment's Terraform does not build it, so no limit is drawn.@@The grey line is max_instances, 1 (too few for a `ceiling-` policy): at it new requests wait or fail with 429.@@

panels.title: Busiest instance's requests (p99, p50)
panels.description: The most requests one instance served at once (`container/max_request_concurrencies`), its 99th and 50th percentile in each 5-minute window. @@E@@The red line is `run-concurrency-high`'s: the p99 above 71.5 for 15 minutes pages. This environment's Terraform does not build it.@@`run-concurrency-high` opens above 71.5, beyond this service's setting, so it never opens for it. The grey line is the concurrency setting, 20: past it a request waits for a slot or a new instance.@@

panels.title: Start-up time (p99, p50)
panels.description: How long a new instance took to start, until it was ready to serve (`container/startup_latencies`): a dot for each interval in which one started. Nothing drawn: no instance started. No policy reads it; a start-up that failed is the last panel.

panels.title: Instances billed
panels.description: Billable instance time per second (`container/billable_instance_time`): how many instances were billed on average. An instance kept warm with CPU always on bills all the time; one that scales to zero, only while it serves.

panels.title: Killed for memory, crashed, failed to start
panels.description: From Cloud Run's own system log: a container killed for exceeding its memory limit (`run_oom_kills`; `run-oom` pages on one), a container that exited with an error or a signal (`run_crash_exits`; `run-crash-loop` at three in fifteen minutes), and a failed start-up or liveness probe (`run_system_errors`; `canary-startup`).

panels.title: cc-db (the staffed desk and svc-voice's hand-off ledger): disk space, CPU, memory, connections, disk I/O
Disk space used (%)
panels.description: How full cc-db's disk is (`database/disk/utilization`), the mean of each 5 minutes. The red line is `cc-db-disk`'s: above 85% for 10 minutes pages. Automatic storage increase grows the disk before it fills, up to the instance's disk_autoresize_limit; at that limit a full disk stops the database taking writes. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing.

panels.title: Disk space: used and size (bytes)
panels.description: cc-db's disk in bytes: used (`database/disk/bytes_used`) and its size (`database/disk/quota`). When the size steps up, Cloud SQL's automatic storage increase grew the disk; it grows only up to disk_autoresize_limit. The dashed red line is 85% of the size, where `cc-db-disk` opens.

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Cloud SQL's `database/up` for cc-db, the lowest in each interval. `cc-db-down` (urgent) pages below 1 for five minutes. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cloud SQL's CPU utilisation for cc-db (`database/cpu/utilization`), the mean of each five minutes, as the monitoring module's policies read it. Their red lines: above 80% for thirty minutes, and above 95% for fifteen (urgent).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Cloud SQL's memory utilisation for cc-db (`database/memory/utilization`), the mean of each five minutes. The red line is the monitoring module's: above 90% for fifteen minutes; past it PostgreSQL's out-of-memory killer restarts the server.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Backends connected (num_backends, summed over the instance's databases), the mean of each minute, as the monitoring module's connection policies read it. @@E@@This environment does not build it, so no limit is drawn.@@Their red lines: above 80 (80% of max_connections) for ten minutes, and above 95 (95%) for five (urgent); max_connections is 100, the grey line, where new connections are refused.@@

panels.title: Disk operations per second
panels.description: cc-db's disk reads and writes per second (`database/disk/read_ops_count`, `write_ops_count`). Reads near none are normal: the working set is in memory.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Bytes cc-db read from and wrote to its disk per second (`database/disk/read_bytes_count`, `write_bytes_count`).

panels.title: Restarts
panels.description: Postgres starting (`sql_restarts`: a crash, a maintenance or a resize restart), counted from Cloud SQL's own logs. Failed backups are in the backups row below.

panels.title: cc-db: backups and point-in-time recovery (seven days of logs)
Backups in the last 30 hours
panels.description: cc-db's successful automated backups in the last 30 hours (`sql_automated_backups`) and its backups or restores that failed (`sql_backup_failures`, a failed automated backup included). One backup a night, starting in a four-hour window from 09:00 UTC: on beta two land up to 26.1 hours apart, so a healthy instance always has one in 30 hours. ✕ none in 30 h, red: none while cc-db reported for 29 of the 30 hours or more (the urgent `cc-db-backup-missing` opens once the day's backup window has passed with none); an instance started since reads "no backup yet". ✕ a backup failed, red, and the failed count red: `cc-db-backup-failed`. ✓ backed up. Point-in-time recovery replays its seven days of logs from a backup taken before the minute chosen. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `cc-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

panels.title: Point-in-time logs (30 min)
panels.description: Cloud SQL's point-in-time logs for cc-db: write-ahead log archives shipped in the last 30 minutes (`database/replication/log_archive_success_count`; about one every five minutes, idle or not) and archives that failed in the last 15 minutes (`log_archive_failure_count`). ✕ stalled, red: none shipped while cc-db reported for 20 of the 30 minutes or more, as the urgent `cc-db-pitr-logs-stalled` opens (ten-minute sums below one held twenty minutes, or nothing reported for thirty): restoring to the minute stops at the last log shipped. ✕ archive failed, red, and the failed count red: `cc-db-pitr-log-archive-failed`. ✓ shipping. Point-in-time recovery keeps seven days of logs. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `cc-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

panels.title: Point-in-time logs shipped, per hour
panels.description: Write-ahead log archives Cloud SQL shipped for cc-db in each hour (`database/replication/log_archive_success_count`): about twelve to fourteen an hour, idle or not. An hour with none is a stall: `cc-db-pitr-logs-stalled` (urgent) opens after 30 minutes with none. "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing.

panels.title: Log archives that failed (15 min)
panels.description: Failed attempts to archive cc-db's write-ahead logs in each 15 minutes (`log_archive_failure_count`), as `cc-db-pitr-log-archive-failed` reads them: any bar opens it. One Cloud SQL retries and recovers from closes it by itself; one that persists stalls the logs.

panels.title: Backups taken, and backups that failed
panels.description: cc-db's successful automated backups, one bar a night in the hour it was counted (`sql_automated_backups`), and backups or restores that failed (`sql_backup_failures`, a failed automated backup included: `cc-db-backup-failed`), per hour. `cc-db-backup-missing` (urgent) opens once a day's backup window has passed with none.

panels.title: The call-centre project: instances against the regional quota, and egress through Cloud NAT (cc-net-nat)
Instances, every service
panels.description: Every Cloud Run instance in the call-centre project, summed. The red line is `run-instances-near-quota`'s: above 68 for 10 minutes pages. The grey line is the regional quota, 85: at it no service can start another instance, whatever its own ceiling.

panels.title: NAT ports: allocated, in use
panels.description: Cloud NAT's ports for the relay's calls to the telephony vendor and svc-voice's to the model: the ports allocated to every instance behind the gateway (`nat/allocated_ports`), and the most connections one instance held to one destination (`nat/port_usage`). In use close to an instance's share of the allocated ports, new connections wait or drop. A cold gateway allocates ports as instances arrive, so the first calls after a quiet spell can wait.

panels.title: NAT new connections
panels.description: New connections Cloud NAT opened for the relay's calls to the telephony vendor and svc-voice's to the model (`nat/new_connections_count`), per interval.

panels.title: NAT dropped packets
panels.description: Packets Cloud NAT dropped in each 5 minutes. Sent, out of ports: an outgoing packet with no port to leave by; the red line is `nat-port-exhaustion`'s, above 10 for 5 minutes. Sent, endpoint conflict: two instances reaching one destination from the same port. Received: replies with no open mapping (a connection already closed); a few are normal.

panels.title: NAT could not allocate
panels.description: Minutes in each 5 in which Cloud NAT could not allocate an address or ports (`nat/nat_allocation_failed`). The red line is `nat-port-exhaustion`'s: above 2 pages.

panels.title: cc-db
panels.description: Cloud SQL's own signals for cc-db: `database/up` (the urgent `cc-db-down` pages below 1 for five minutes) and disk used (`cc-db-disk` at 85% for ten minutes). "database stopped": stopped on purpose between test sessions (beta's database_activation_policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing.

panels.title: migrate-cc executions
panels.description: cc-db's schema migration, run by a person (staffed desk only). A failure opens `jobs-failed`.
